title: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: the Bible was written for our learning.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We have to have patience with our people, because they get upset. They have never heard this truth before: Jesus Christ is black, the Israelites are black, the Puerto Ricans are the tribe of Ephraim. So we have to be patient with them.

And the comfort of the scriptures: it is a comfort to know that we are God's chosen people, that being black is something to be proud of, that there is honour in being dark skinned, black like Jesus Christ, the black Messiah. We comfort our people with these scriptures.

And there is hope in these scriptures. We are not going to win against an imperialist US government, or any government for that matter, with arms, bombs and guns. It is not going to happen. Through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope: we go into the scriptures, deal with our people patiently, comfort them, and show them who they are according to the Bible.

precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read.” We have to seek out of the book of the Lord and read for ourselves. When the scriptures are brought to our people, they have to read them for themselves, because a man could be lying, a man could be wrong, but the scriptures don't lie. The scriptures are where you find the truth, the hope, the comfort.

“No one of these shall fail”: these prophecies shall not fail. The prophecy of what would happen to the tribe of Ephraim in these last days will not fail, and we have the history, the books, to back it up.

“None shall want her mate.” A lot of books are brought out in this class, but if a book does not align with the scriptures, it is not brought out. They are brought out because they line up with what the scriptures say.

“Blessed is he that readeth.” For a long time our family members, and we ourselves, went to church and just sat there and let the pastor give us his spiel, his rhetoric, and never read the scriptures for ourselves to see whether what he brought out was true. Blessed is he that readeth, because he does not get deceived; he does not get lied to.

“And they that hear the words of this prophecy”: the prophecy of Jesus Christ, the black Messiah. “And keep those things which are written therein”: we have to keep what is written. “For the time is at hand.”

“I Daniel understood by books.” Daniel got his understanding by books. So in this class the books are brought out, historical records together with the Bible, to show who the tribe of Ephraim is, who Jesus Christ the black Messiah is, and who the damn devil is that deceived us and gave us a white Jesus and a white God, which are not found in the Bible.

But if a book does not coincide with what the scriptures say, don't follow it.

“Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel”: unto his people Israel. Not everybody. The people of God is Israel, the nation.

“There hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.” The Bible is a true book. Everything that comes out of it is true: it has come to pass and it is coming to pass. Everything he told Moses, and Moses told us, came to pass. So we have to read for ourselves: he that readeth shall be blessed.

sense.text:
Do we need the books? No. Before the internet, before Google, the bishops and the elders before them identified who the northern kingdom is according to the scriptures: by the curses that are upon our people today. The books only back up what the scriptures say.

“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” This is spoken to the tribe of Ephraim, the so-called Puerto Ricans, and to all the tribes; today is Ephraim's turn, because of all the questions and comments that came in.

All these curses come upon the nation of Israel and overtake them. This is how we know who the twelve tribes are: the curses are upon the nation of Israel till this day.

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” These curses are upon us for a sign. When we see these curses upon us, when we go through these conditions, it is a sign to tell us who we are.

We're not black. We're not Latino. We're not Native American. We're not Puerto Rican. We're not even Boricua. We're the nation of Israel, and the so-called Puerto Ricans are the tribe of Ephraim. And upon thy seed: upon our children, for ever.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.” You want to know how you got to Puerto Rico, that little island? The Most High scattered you there.

The twelve tribes of Israel are scattered, and the Bible documents that scattering of the twelve tribes.

sense.text:
Roman Catholicism is the main religion in Puerto Rico, close to 70% of the people, with about 25% more in the Protestant and evangelical churches, all of which fall under Catholicism, the umbrella of the man-made religions. Roman: the Romans are a people, the so-called white people, so it is Caucasian Catholicism, with a white Jesus, a white God and white saints. It came by force: Atahualpa was burned at the stake for not accepting a white Jesus. The cacique, the leader, the king, was Christianized: the cacique of the monument was baptized Don Alonso el Manso, manso meaning tamed, docile, weak, like a tamed horse. The monument's own inscription says the Catholic evangelization of the Taíno served as a significant tool in the conquest of Borikén: a tool is a weapon, like the gun and the rifle. After the rebellion of 1511 the Taínos were defeated by the conquistadors, and Juan Ponce de León, after whom Ponce is named, granted a dispensation to those who accepted Christianity, letting them live as lesser than what they are, which is caciques, kings. There is nothing honourable about humiliating our kings, stripping them of their heritage and giving them something demonic like the Roman Catholic religion.

The conquistadors are found in the scriptures. “And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow”: he had weapons, tools. “And a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer.” Conquering: conquistador. This man on a white horse represents Esau conquering the dark nations.

It is our history, what we went through: dogs sicked on us, our women ravaged, raped and cut open, hands and noses chopped off, our people forced to eat the hands of our own people, our babies burned, our people tortured, whipped and hanged. That is the so-called Roman Catholic religion. Demons. The Pope and Esau today come from those forefathers; that is what they did to us, and there is nothing good about these people.

All of this came upon our people for accepting the Roman Catholic religion, for trusting the so-called white man, and for turning our backs on God's laws. These are the curses that befell our people. And seeing all these atrocities done to the northern kingdom, the so-called Latinos, is what qualifies them for this heritage. Hebrew Israelites who discount the Latinos because of light skin and different shades of brown have the same mentality as the white man, no different from Esau.

The histories say who the conqueror is. Dr. William Smith's Dictionary of the Bible, written in 1890, when we were just coming out of slavery in Puerto Rico, says that from Edom proceeded the kings who reigned in Italy and built up Rome, that Italy and Greece and all the western provinces were filled with Idumeans, and that the prophets called that whole nation by the name of Edom. It says that by Edom is meant Rome, and that all the prophets said about the destruction of Edom in the last times refers to Rome. The medieval chroniclers say expressly that Edom means the Roman Empire, or the European powers, and Benjamin of Tudela, around 1160, called Rome the Edomite capital and the Pope the head of the Edomitish religion. Those are the Italians, the Romans, the Roman Catholic popes: the so-called white men are the nation of Edom. Esau wrote about himself, and that is why they did not allow us to read or write.

John Allen's Modern Judaism sets down the traditions about Esau's descendants: that the sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob, even to the end of the world, were at first a small nation inhabiting Mount Seir, but after the twelve tribes were destroyed by the Assyrians and Babylonians they increased, subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire, overturned the Jewish state when the second temple was destroyed by Titus, were the first of all nations to embrace the religion of Jesus of Nazareth, and hold the dominion over all Europe, detaining Jacob in captivity till the Messiah, the son of David, shall appear. And that the prophecies of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah against Esau have not yet received their full accomplishment: the final vengeance for the destruction of the second temple is yet to be executed in the time of the Messiah, against Edom, which belongs to Rome and the Christians, and the slaughter of the Christians in the future battle will be greater than that of the Turks.

They took the Bible and made their own man-made religion, Christianity, Catholicism, and forced it upon us. So when the historians wrote Christians they meant the nation of Esau, and the prophecies against Esau have not yet been fulfilled: Esau has not yet been destroyed and is still in power to this day, and we are still in captivity until Christ returns and delivers us. But Obadiah says there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau. We're not deceived any longer. We know who our enemy is.

Roman Catholicism came to the island of Puerto Rico with the conquistadors, Ponce de León and Christopher Columbus.

“Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth”: we say we love God, we say Jesus Christ is our Lord and Saviour, amen, hallelujah. “And with their lips do honour me”: with our lips we honour Christ. “But have removed their heart far from me”: we have removed our minds far from Christ, far from what the scriptures say, and we do idol worship.

That is why you have black priests with white men on the cross, and our people kissing statues of white people: a white man walking around bloody with ketchup on, and a Puerto Rican woman who really thinks that is Jesus Christ, balling, crying tears. More black people worshipping a white man, in Panama too. Our people are so easily deceived because of centuries and centuries of lies forced upon them: if we did not accept it, we were put to death, burned at the stake. We were in idolatry before, but not to white men, not to that extent. That is what happens when you accept Roman Catholicism.

precepts.why:
Christ is quoting what was just read in Isaiah: “This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.” Our people draw near unto Christ with their mouth, but their minds are far from him. Even Christ said it back then.

“But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.” What that translates to this day is Roman Catholicism, Christianity, a white man Jesus and a white man God. Doctrines of devils, far from Christ.

The man-made religions all came the same way: John Smith made the Baptist religion in 1608, while we were in slavery; Joseph Smith the Mormon religion in 1830; William Miller the Seventh-day Adventist religion; Charles T. Russell the Jehovah's Witnesses in 1872; Charles Parham the Pentecostal religion in 1901. And Pope Nicholas V, of the popes our people venerate and look upon as God on earth, is the father of the transatlantic slave trade. All Edomite religions, all descended from the Roman Catholic Church, and none of it is found in the scriptures. The Bible is the Israelites' history book, our laws, statutes and commandments. It has nothing to do with Esau.

sense.text:
This is why that so-called Puerto Rican at the camp wanted to fight the elder and Captain Abiel when they stepped on the image of Caesar Borgia.

“As the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty”: the same way the devil tricked Eve, through his subtilty, his tricks. “So your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ”: our minds are corrupted from the simplicity. Christ is easy to understand if you read for yourself.

“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus.” Who came preaching another Jesus? The conquistadors: Christopher Columbus, Ponce de León, Hernán Cortés, white men who came with the Catholic religion. And the priests were not far behind. They were needed to indoctrinate the people: Christianity, Catholicism, was used as a tool to make our people docile. That is why they baptized the cacique Don Alonso as el manso, the tame. Esau knew how to control our people with the religion he created.

And look at the fruit of it: 1923 Christmas cards with our people on them, and a Christian church pulpit with a priest on it and the KKK around him, the KKK that was burning and lynching black people, Israelites. Yet now we think we can be united with them in the same church building, the same religion; that there are good white people. Hell to the no.

“Never trust thine enemy.” The Bible tells us never trust thine enemy. When the conquistadors came, when the priests came with that religion, we were not supposed to trust them. “For like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself”: though he come bearing gifts in the name of Christianity, the white man's religion. “And go crouching”: there you see the Pope crouching. “Yet take good heed and beware of him.” Now they come with smiles and docile ways, but in their hearts, in their minds, there is nothing but evil, death and destruction towards our people.

That is how Catholicism was forced upon us: they came with their Catholic priests and baptized the so-called Taínos, the Boricuas. Never trust thine enemies. Now in Puerto Rico our people kneel with rosary beads to the white image of the Virgin Mary and the baby Jesus, with the saints behind them as white people. That is idolatry, and that is what happens when you accept the white man's religion: you become docile, you become stupid, you become dumb, you become slaves.

The image of Christ cannot be taught enough, because our people have the white man's religion and the white man's image in their heads. In the Pillory, the book the Bishop brings out almost every Sabbath, shows it: the bust of the Saviour was posed for by Caesar Borgia, the bastard son of Pope Alexander VI. It is an open secret: Esau knows the truth, but it was kept secret from us, because we were not allowed to read, and now they make these books so expensive we can't afford them. That is how Ephraim got that image in his head, and why that so-called Puerto Rican got so upset when the image was stomped on. That lie has to be cleared out of our people's minds.

Some doubted when the image was taught, saying it is a similitude, an allegory, or that Christ in his glory has to be white. That makes no sense, and the scriptures clear it up.

“The Revelation of Jesus Christ”: the revealing of Jesus Christ, “which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John.” John the Revelator wrote it down.
“Who bare record of the word of God, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” He bore record: everything that he saw was written down.

“Blessed is he that readeth”: blessed is he that reads those records for himself, so that he is not deceived by a white image. “And keep those things which are written therein”: with this Bible you cannot be deceived. You can cast down wicked imaginations and doctrines.

“I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last”: this is Jesus the Christ when he appeared unto John the Revelator. “What thou seest, write in a book”: Christ told him to write what he saw, because in the last days one would come preaching another Jesus. So Christ had to leave his image recorded for us in these last days.

“And send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia”: Asia here is Greece. Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. The Bishop, Deacon Malachi and other leaders have visited the churches in Ephesus and Smyrna; the acts of the apostles still continue to this day. And those churches were not white people: at this time we were scattered in Asia.

“And I turned to see the voice that spake with me”: John turned to see who was talking to him. “And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks”: he saw a menorah. He did not see a crucifix; he did not see a cross. A seven-branch menorah, not an eight or nine branch, and the seven branches represent the seven churches.

“One like unto the Son of man”: in the midst of that seven-branch menorah he saw Christ. Our people say the image doesn't matter, it doesn't matter what Christ looks like, as long as I have him in my heart, as long as I believe, I shall be saved. But if you don't know what Jesus Christ looks like, you are going to get deceived and fall for a white man Jesus. Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, vain lies.

“Clothed with a garment down to the foot”: Jesus Christ had a body with a garment. He is not a spirit, not a puff of smoke. Jesus Christ is a black man.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool”: wool, like the woolly hair of the negro. Some of the old dictionaries define woolly as the hair of the negro, because the writers back then knew what woolly meant. Our people say wool means white, but it says white like wool: it tells two things, the colour and the texture. The colour is white; the texture is wool. Who has woolly hair to this day? The so-called black people, the so-called Puerto Ricans.

The original slave registries kept in Puerto Rico show it. Each one gave the slave's height, colour, hair, beard, eyes, nose and mouth. Modesto, a boy of about fifteen, was dark skinned with an afro, woolly hair, black eyes and a large nose. Lucia, eighty years old and still labouring in the fields, was dark skinned with a flat nose. Manuel, who came directly from Africa, was dark with an afro. There were black Puerto Ricans, black Ephraimites. Ephraim is a cake not turned, so the Puerto Ricans come from the lightest shade, almost white, to the darkest dark, like Roberto Clemente. Not all Ephraim is light skinned.

Manuel coming from Africa does not make him Judah. The twelve tribes are scattered to the four corners, and in Puerto Rico would be found the tribe of Ephraim. The European slave traders were well informed about the African ethnicities and targeted the groups the plantation owners preferred, so those groups were concentrated in certain parts of the Americas. They knew who they were picking up: give me the tribe of Ephraim for my plantation in Puerto Rico. That is how we know those dark-skinned slaves were of the tribe of Ephraim.

“And his eyes were as a flame of fire.” That tripped up Carlos, the host of The Theology of the Streets, who asked whether it was literal or figurative. Christ drank wine. Jesus Christ did not have blue eyes and did not have blonde hair; he had an afro, white like wool. The image shown is not an exact image of Jesus Christ, but a more accurate depiction according to the scriptures.

“And his feet like unto fine brass”: this is not the image in Daniel. John said one like unto the Son of man, so this is describing Jesus Christ's feet. People forget that bronze is a derivative of brown, the third colour of the Olympic medals, gold, silver and bronze.

“As if they burned in a furnace”: burn anything, especially brass, and it turns black. Jesus Christ's feet were so black they looked like they burned in a furnace. The brass menorah burned in the fire shows it: the brass turns black. Christ looked like burned brass. That is easy to understand.

“And his voice as the sound of many waters”: he had a deep voice. That is hip talk, like teeth white with milk. The scriptures talk that way: when the king was rich it says he waxed fat; when Saul went to relieve himself it says he covered his feet. That is how you know the scriptures were written by black people, Israelites, hip people that use slang. We speak in parables; we get that from Christ and from the prophets. Our people have to stop being simple-minded.

precepts.why:
Who was in Ephesus? Those were not white people. “Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.” Paul writes to the saints, and the scriptures show who the saints are.

“Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.” Paul is addressing the Israelites that are in Ephesus. “Who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.”

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ.” People say, you see, all nations can be adopted. No. Paul clears up who the adoption is for in Romans 9. Line upon line, here a little, there a little: this is how you get the understanding. A lot of the so-called Puerto Rican Catholics don't know how to read the Bible line upon line.

Some say the saints are white people, the saints are anybody. “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The horn of his people is Jesus the Christ, and the saints are the children of Israel: the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans who are under the curses of Deuteronomy 28:15-68. So the saints at Ephesus, in the churches of Asia, were Israelites.

There may be new people watching who have never heard this truth, so we have to be patient and comfort them with the scriptures, so that they too may have hope.

“For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”: my brethren, my relatives, my kinsmen, my family, blood relation. According to the flesh: Israelite flesh, black flesh, Latinos, Native Americans. We are family; we are the nation of Israel.

“Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption.” Paul was talking to the twelve tribes of Israel that were scattered in Asia, and that is who the adoption is for. The adoption is not for everyone; the adoption is for the Israelites. Don't let the wicked of our people deceive you; don't get rocked back to sleep. Keep these precepts so that you remember: write them down, study them.

Carlos asked whether the eyes as a flame of fire were literal or figurative, and our people don't know, so we have to educate them. “His eyes shall be red with wine”: when you drink wine, the whites of your eyes turn red. Christ drank wine. Jesus Christ did not have blue eyes.

“And his teeth white with milk.” That one caught him up. Captain Abiel told him yes, his teeth were white with milk: Christ's teeth were white. And what the milk represents, line upon line, is shown in 1 Peter.

“As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word.” The milk is the word. So Jesus Christ's teeth were white with milk because he came teaching the laws. That is what the white like milk represents.

Line upon line, here a little and there a little: this is how you get the understanding, and it is not for everybody to understand. If you are not keeping the commandments, if you go by a white man Jesus and what the Christian pastors teach you, you are going to get confused.

sense.text: “And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came.” Joseph is the father of the two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. At this time he was in Egypt, where his brothers had sold him into slavery because they were jealous of him: he was his father's favourite.
“For God, said he, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.” That is what Manasseh means: made to forget.

“And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.” Ephraim is who we are dealing with. One of the blessings of Ephraim, the so-called Puerto Ricans, is to have many, many children.
“I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath shewed me also thy seed.” Israel, the father of the twelve tribes, saw his son Joseph, whom he thought was dead and never to be seen again.

Joseph brought his two sons out to his father Israel and bowed himself with his face to the earth. He took “Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand”, because Manasseh was the oldest, and he wanted Israel to bless the oldest with his right hand.

“And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger”: he crossed his hands. “Guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn”: he knew what he was doing. He knew Manasseh was the firstborn, but he gave the first blessing unto Ephraim.

“Bless the lads; and let my name be named on them.” This is why Ephraim and Manasseh, even though they are Joseph's children, became part of the twelve tribes of the nation of Israel. “And let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.”

When Joseph saw his father's right hand upon Ephraim's head, “it displeased him”, because the blessing went first to the youngest, and the blessing usually goes to the firstborn, which was Manasseh. So he held up his father's hand to move it unto Manasseh's head: “Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head.”

“I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.” Ephraim's seed is a multitude of nations.

That is what is seen today. As of 2024 to 2026, roughly 64% to 67% of the people of Puerto Rican origin live in the fifty states and the District of Columbia, about 6.1 million, and only about 3.2 to 3.3 million on the island. That is displacement, and it shows Ephraim scattered, a multitude of nations, scattered throughout the United States; you find Ephraimites even in Hawaii.

And it is by design. There are abandoned buildings all over Puerto Rico, and investors come to buy them up: they intend for Ephraim to abandon the island so they can come and buy everything. Back then the Assyrians and the Babylonians moved us out of the land and replaced us with other nations; now Esau deals with us subtly. They say there's no work, come to the United States; they paint it as the land of milk and honey, and our people get deceived.

Where our people are taking over the abandoned places, cleaning them and growing food, that is what we have to do. We can't let Esau come and take our lands and our houses. We have to put our foot down, set an example, be leaders in our communities: take over the house, fix it up, have some self-worth, and not wait on Esau for the welfare check. Plant, grow. Unity is what is missing in our communities: community is common unity, having all things in common, like in Acts 2 and Acts 4.
“God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.” Ephraim is the head tribe of the northern kingdom.

The curses are upon the tribe of Ephraim, the nation of Israel. “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.” Christianity and Islam are the two main religions our people are in. This is being scattered, displaced, exiled from your lands. The gentrification going on in Puerto Rico is not by coincidence; it is by design.

In 1947 Puerto Rico's legislature passed Public Law 89, and a year later the migration division opened: not a job fair, a state-run pipeline. By the late 1960s over 60,000 a year were being shipped to mainland farms. Shipped: you shall be scattered, with ships. In the 1500s and 1600s it was slavery; now it is the workforce in the United States. They did it to Ephraim in Hawaii too, sending them to work the sugarcane fields; that is why there is a lot of Ephraim in Hawaii.

In Lorain, Ohio our people followed the work to the steel mills, built churches, opened bodegas and raised families. Then the mills closed, urban renewal bulldozed their blocks, and the community the US government engineered into existence was allowed to vanish from the map: recruited, used and erased, as if Ephraim never existed there. That is what goes on with our people: they use us, abuse us, and then act like we don't exist.

That is why we have to come out of her, my people, and be not partakers of her sins. Especially Ephraim, because a lot of Ephraim blend in, start speaking that good English, and forget their people and who they are. But just because you are light skinned, Esau knows: he kept well-manicured records of his slaves, his property. Even if you are light skinned, the curses fit you. You're an Israelite.

“Afterward saw I the same man come down from the mountain, and call unto him another peaceable Multitude.” The same man is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, read of in Revelation 1:14: feet like burned brass, hair like wool. He called unto him another peaceable multitude.

The historians knew who that peaceable multitude was. Lost Tribes and Promised Lands by Ronald Sanders, written in 1978 and brought out by the bishops and the elders in the early nineties, says Columbus gave the peaceable multitude of the islands the name Indios because he considered their habitation to be the Indies, but perhaps also because he thought of them as living in God: en Dios. They called us noble savages, but the scriptures call them a peaceable multitude, and Columbus was reading the book of Ezra. In God is better than savages.

precepts.why:
“And whereas thou sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude unto him; Those are the ten tribes.” The northern kingdom of the nation of Israel: that is who Christ gathered, and who he is going to gather in these last days.

How? Through the work the prophets are doing, the worldwide blitzes going on in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Mexico and Chile, to our brothers and sisters scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

sense.text:
A lot of the so-called Puerto Ricans say we were with the Taínos, we always been here, this is our land. No: our land is Israel, and this shows how the ten tribes got to this side of the world.

“Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”: the Assyrian captivity, 722 BC. “And he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land”: into Assyria. We were forcefully displaced then; now it is through subtilty.

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen”: this is a jump in history to the Persian captivity, when Cyrus the Persian gave us freedom to leave. “And go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”: a land that was not populated.

“That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” The northern kingdom wanted a fresh start. They were tired of captivity after captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, so when they were given freedom they went to a further country where never mankind dwelt, where they might keep God's commandments.

“And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river.” What is read here is what is seen on the map: the journey of the ten tribes to North America, South America, the Caribbean, the islands of the sea.

“For the most High then shewed signs for them”: Issachar was good in navigation; they read the stars and knew which way to go and where the sea was calm. “And held still the flood, till they were passed over”: he held still the waters, because it was not just one ship. It was hundreds and hundreds of ships, thousands and thousands of our people of the ten tribes, gathering food, clothes and gold for the journey.

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half.” It took a year and a half because we made stops along the routes: Madagascar, South Africa, Angola; Brazil, where some of Asher were dropped off; some of Naphtali into Argentina, Peru, Colombia; the Caribbean, where Manasseh and Ephraim were dropped off; Florida, where Reuben was dropped off; North America and Canada, the tribe of Gad. It was not an overnight thing. It was a process.

“And the same region is called Arsareth.” This is for the so-called Puerto Ricans who don't know who they are; there is no more excuse after this. The Jewish Encyclopedia, written by Jewish historians, not black people, says Arsareth is the land beyond the great river, far away from the habitation of men, in which the ten tribes of Israel dwell observing the laws of Moses until the time of restoration, when Jesus Christ returns and restores all things to the nation of Israel; and that Columbus identified America with this land. Columbus knew who was here.

The European writers knew it too. Huddleston's Origins of the American Indians: European Concepts, 1492 to 1729, gives Lumnius' argument that the ten tribes exiled by Salmanasar escaped to Arsareth, which he identified as India: America. Durán found confirmation in Hosea, God's promise to multiply Israel, fulfilled by the multitudes the Spanish found in the new world; and the Indians of Mexico, the tribe of Issachar, had traditions of long journeys like the one from Assyria to Arsareth, of the flight out of Egypt, of earthquakes that swallowed evil men and manna falling from heaven, and an old Indian began the tale of his people's origins with the words, in the beginning. Why would so-called Indians be quoting the Bible unless they were Israelites? We had books; we carried the Bible with us.

In Lost Tribes and Promised Lands, Montezinos, a Marrano, an Israelite of Spain forced to convert to Christianity, met so-called Indians who told him, in their common ancestral tongue, Hebrew, that they were of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. The tribe of Joseph is Ephraim and Manasseh: the so-called Puerto Ricans and Cubans. Francisco, the Indian translator, said his own people had made war on them to their eternal shame, Israelites warring with Israelites; that they were a special people, God's chosen people; that the God of these children of Israel is the true God and everything inscribed on their tablets is true. We had records; they stole our records and took our books. Montezinos turned it into propaganda for the Dutch conquest of Brazil, to go after the riches of the ten tribes.

The book Christopher Columbus and the Participation of the Jews says Columbus was very fond of reading the Bible and the fourth book of Ezra, and that what drove him was not a love of science but the prophecies: he knew this side of the world was populated with the ten tribes of Israel. Writers had already shown in the sixteenth century that the natives were descended from the Jews, and Roldán held that the language of Hispaniola, Cuba, Jamaica and the islands was a corrupted Hebrew: Cuba and Haiti are Hebrew names, and the names of their rivers and persons, drawn from Jonah, Jacob, Urias and Moses, and of their canoes, their pepper and their storehouses for grain, all point to the Hebrew language. They spoke Hebrew, corrupted over years and years in captivity.

When the Bishop and the deacons put boots on the ground in Puerto Rico in 2017, they met Dr. Reniel Rodríguez, a professor of archaeology, holding ancient relics found in Puerto Rico with Hebrew writing etched in them, something that would change the history of Puerto Rico; scholars try to deny it, and the relics are kept in a bin at a university. Hebrew writings in Puerto Rico. Don't tell me the so-called Puerto Ricans are not the tribe of Ephraim.

precepts.why:
Cyrus gave the ten tribes their freedom because of the prophecy. “Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”: the Most High moved Cyrus, in 539 BC. “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”

“Who is there among you of all his people?” His people: not Persians, Israelites, God's people. “Let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel.” Cyrus gave us freedom to go back to Jerusalem and build the house of God.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth”: whether we were in Assyria or in Persia, wherever we were scattered and displaced, we were given freedom to go back. That is the history behind what 2 Esdras 13 says: with that freedom the ten tribes took counsel to leave the multitude of the heathen and go into a further country.

sense.text: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.” The last days are from the time Christ walked the earth until now.

“Joseph is a fruitful bough”: that is one of the symbols of the tribe of Ephraim, because the blessing upon Ephraim is many children. That is why millions are scattered throughout the United States and fewer are left in Puerto Rico. “Even a fruitful bough by a well”: there are many riches in Puerto Rico, in the waters.

“Whose branches run over the wall”: that is race mixing. What wall? El Morro. Our women, in desperation, because they did not keep the faith and the commandments, mixed with the Spaniards to survive, to try to find a better life. In some Bibles there is a note on branches that reads daughters: the daughters of Ephraim and the daughters of Manasseh ran over the wall to mix with the conquistadors, the Spaniards.

The Flame of Resistance, the book that inspired the title of this class, tells an old Latin American legend of a foreign tyrant who tried to bury the truth. That tyrant is Esau. He used arms to conquer another nation, and Christianity, the Roman Catholic religion; he enslaved the people and forced them to work for his benefit on the sugar and coffee plantations; he could never have enough wealth and power. But the truth stood in his way, so he ordered the people to give it up, shot or jailed those who refused, as in the uprisings at Jayuya and Ponce, and buried the truth in a deep hole. That is why we are called the hidden ones: they tried to hide us from the world, keep us from reading, and push us into Catholicism. But two peasants dug it up, and all that remained was a small seed, which they planted as they would plant a corn seed; and on that spot grew a strong and beautiful tree.

That is the purpose of the missions and the worldwide blitzes: to plant the seed of truth in the minds and hearts of our people and wait for God to give the increase. Ephraim is a fruitful tree planted by the waters. We have to keep the commandments; that is how the truth will grow and prosper. That is what the evil tyrant Esau fears.

“The archers have sorely grieved him.” That is who the branches ran over the wall to: the archers, the conquistadors, the rider with the bow on the white horse in Revelation 6:2. “And shot at him”: they shot the men, the Ephraimites, the warriors, the caciques. They burned us at the stake, tortured us, cut our limbs, raped our women and killed our elders. “And hated him”: they hated us because we are God's chosen people, and they wanted our land and our riches.

“But his bow abode in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the mighty God of Jacob.” “From thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel”: that shepherd is Christ, and the stone, the rock of Israel, is Christ.

“Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee; and by the Almighty, who shall bless thee with blessings of heaven above”: the good weather of Puerto Rico. It is an island paradise; that is why a lot of the southern kingdom wanted to keep the Passover there. “Blessings of the deep that lieth under”: there are many riches in the waters.

“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last.” God is sending his apostles last. Before us came Pedro Albizu Campos, Blanca Canales, Lolita Lebrón, Filiberto Ojeda Ríos, the Young Lords, all the brothers and sisters who paved the way for the truth to come out and fought for our rights. It was not just the southern kingdom: the northern kingdom was fighting as well.

Pedro Albizu Campos, El Maestro, was of the tribe of Ephraim. He loved his people: they imprisoned him, tortured him and did experiments on him, and the Pope himself offered him the governorship of Puerto Rico if he would give up his revolutionary ways, and he said he could not betray his people. Brothers like him, like Fred Hampton, are believed to be prophets back on the earth: they did not have the truth in their time, but the Most High will show them mercy for their works and the love they had for their people. Albizu Campos passed away April 21, 1965, and four days later there was a revolution in the Dominican Republic. There were always revolts in Cuba, Haiti, the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico, because we are not a people that is supposed to be enslaved or indoctrinated.

So the Most High left the apostles last, as it is to this day. People will laugh at the men in purple and gold and say they don't know what they're talking about, but the scriptures prove who we are. God left the truth so that we can find it and plant the seeds in the hearts and minds of our people. We have a big job to do: all this is to inspire the northern kingdom, the tribe of Ephraim, the twelve tribes of Israel, to do the work.
